answer: Follow the copper. Every reward is tagged, and the ledger traces where it travels for 30 epochs. When twenty keys keep sweeping earnings into one wallet, that shared thread is a stronger signal than any writing style, so the cluster's future rewards drop to one key's share until an appeal shows separate operators. Laundering through extra hops costs fees (estimate: 1-2% per hop, assuming typical swap fees) and eats the farm's margin. Tradeoff: honest owners who pool funds get flagged, so they can declare their keys up front and accept one shared cap.
